inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that the government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything.” This complaint really exposes how corporations resist accountability for the plastic bottles found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains. It underscores the structural problem where big business externalizes its costs onto the rest of society, piling environmental harm onto vulnerable groups who already face the worst effects of inequality and lack the power to demand better. We need real institutional reform so taxes actually force companies to fund protections and cleanup instead of letting profits come before people and the planet.
inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters is exactly right to complain that the government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything.” This is just another example of big government grabbing money from productive businesses while failing to enforce basic order or personal responsibility. Instead of businesses somehow being responsible for plastic bottles turning up everywhere and blocking rivers and drains, the real issue is individuals who discard their waste without any sense of duty to their community or the nation. We do not need more institutional reform or taxes to punish companies and force them into progressive schemes that put profits last. What we need is a return to cultural standards where people take care of their own messes, respect authority, and stop expecting the state or corporations to clean up after a breakdown in family values and self-reliance.
